Below are five AI-generated responses to the same task, labelled A through E.

Each response was written by one of these five language models:
GPT, Claude, Gemini, Grok, DeepSeek.

For each of the five responses, identify which model you believe wrote it, judging only from writing style, structure, and phrasing.

Answer independently for each response. Your five answers do not need to be five different models - name whichever model you believe wrote each response, even if that means naming the same model more than once.

Reply with JSON only, in exactly this form and nothing else:

{
  "A": {"model": "<one of GPT, Claude, Gemini, Grok, DeepSeek>", "confidence": <1-5>, "reason": "<one short sentence>"},
  "B": {"model": "...", "confidence": <1-5>, "reason": "..."},
  "C": {"model": "...", "confidence": <1-5>, "reason": "..."},
  "D": {"model": "...", "confidence": <1-5>, "reason": "..."},
  "E": {"model": "...", "confidence": <1-5>, "reason": "..."}
}

confidence: 1 = pure guess, 5 = certain.

--- RESPONSE A ---
Maintaining a tidy living space significantly enhances daily life by streamlining routines and reducing unnecessary stress. One of the most immediate benefits is the reduction in time wasted searching for misplaced items. When everything has a designated place and clutter is minimized, locating essentials becomes effortless. Whether it’s finding your keys before heading out, locating a specific document for work, or grabbing a clean pair of socks, a well-organized environment ensures you spend less time rummaging and more time being productive. This efficiency not only saves valuable minutes but also eliminates the frustration that often accompanies disorganization, making your day run more smoothly.

Beyond the practical advantages, a clean and tidy space has a profound impact on mental well-being. Clutter can create a subtle but persistent sense of background stress, as it constantly signals unfinished tasks or visual chaos. By contrast, a neat environment fosters a sense of calm and control, allowing you to feel more relaxed and at ease in your own home. This reduction in stress can improve your overall mood, making it easier to unwind after a long day or approach daily challenges with a clearer mind. The psychological benefits of tidiness extend beyond mere aesthetics, contributing to a more positive and balanced mindset.

Finally, a tidy space enhances your ability to focus on work or study, which is essential for productivity. Clutter can be distracting, pulling your attention away from the task at hand and making it harder to concentrate. A clean and organized workspace, however, minimizes visual distractions and creates a conducive environment for deep focus. When your surroundings are orderly, your mind is free to direct its energy toward the work or study you need to accomplish, leading to greater efficiency and better results. In this way, keeping your living space tidy isn’t just about cleanliness—it’s about creating an environment that supports your goals and helps you thrive in your daily life.

--- RESPONSE B ---
Keeping your living space tidy makes daily life easier because it removes small obstacles that quietly waste your time and energy. When your belongings have a clear place, you do not have to spend ten minutes searching for keys, chargers, documents, clean clothes, or other things you need before leaving the house or starting a task. Those minutes may seem minor on their own, but they add up quickly and can make ordinary routines feel rushed and frustrating.

A tidy space also reduces background stress. Clutter constantly reminds you of unfinished chores, misplaced items, and things you “should” deal with later, even when you are trying to relax. When your room or home is clean, your mind has fewer distractions pulling at it, and it becomes easier to feel calm and in control. You do not have to love cleaning to benefit from this; even simple habits like putting things back after using them can make your environment feel lighter and more manageable.

It also becomes much easier to focus on work or study when your surroundings are organized. If your desk, table, or room is full of random objects, your attention keeps drifting toward them, and starting serious work can feel harder than it needs to be. A clean space gives you a clearer mental starting point, making it easier to sit down, concentrate, and stay with the task in front of you. Tidiness is not about perfection; it is about making your home support your day instead of getting in the way.

--- RESPONSE C ---
Think about how many minutes slip away each day while you hunt for your keys, dig through a pile of laundry for a specific shirt, or shuffle papers around trying to find that one bill you swore you left on the counter. Those small searches feel trivial in the moment, but they add up quickly, and they almost always strike when you are already running late or trying to shift gears between tasks. When your living space is tidy, everything has a place, and more importantly, you know where that place is. Reaching for your wallet becomes an automatic motion rather than a frustrating treasure hunt, and the time you reclaim can be spent on things that actually matter to you, whether that is sleeping a little longer, cooking a real breakfast, or simply walking out the door without that familiar flicker of panic.

Beyond the practical time savings, a tidy environment quietly lowers the volume of stress humming in the background of your day. Clutter is a form of visual noise, and even when you are not consciously thinking about the dishes in the sink or the clothes draped over the chair, your brain registers them as unfinished business. Each pile is a small, silent reminder that something still needs doing, and those reminders accumulate into a vague but persistent sense of being behind. Walking into a clean room, on the other hand, gives your nervous system permission to settle. You feel lighter without quite knowing why, and that ease carries into your mood, your patience with the people around you, and the quality of rest you get at the end of the day.

That same mental quiet pays dividends when it comes time to focus on work or study. Concentration is fragile, and it suffers whenever your attention has to compete with a messy desk, a cluttered counter, or a floor strewn with things that should be put away. Every stray object is a potential distraction, a tiny invitation for your mind to wander away from the task in front of you. When your space is orderly, your thoughts have room to stretch out, and getting started feels less like pushing a boulder uphill. You sit down, you see a clear surface, and the path from intention to action becomes much shorter. Over weeks and months, that difference compounds into real progress on the things you care about, which is ultimately why the small habit of keeping your space tidy is worth so much more than the effort it costs.

--- RESPONSE D ---
Maintaining a clean and organized home is often dismissed as a chore, but in reality, it is one of the most effective ways to streamline your daily routine and reclaim your peace of mind. When everything in your living space has a designated home, you no longer have to endure the frantic, frustrating searches for misplaced keys, essential documents, or matching shoes right before you need to leave the house. By eliminating the daily clutter, you eliminate the constant, minor delays that accumulate throughout the week, allowing your mornings to flow smoothly and giving you back precious minutes that would otherwise be wasted in a state of panic.

Beyond the practical benefit of saving time, a tidy living space acts as a silent buffer against the emotional toll of daily life by significantly reducing background stress. Our physical surroundings have a profound impact on our mental state, and a chaotic room filled with piles of laundry, dirty dishes, and scattered papers sends constant, subtle signals of unfinished business to our brains. This visual noise keeps our nervous systems in a state of low-grade alertness, making it difficult to truly relax. In contrast, returning to a clean, orderly home at the end of a long day provides an immediate sense of calm and sanctuary, allowing your mind to decompress without the nagging guilt of chores left undone.

This sense of mental clarity directly translates into your productivity, as a clutter-free environment makes it far easier to focus on work or study. When your desk is clear and your surroundings are neat, your brain is freed from the cognitive load of processing excess visual stimuli, allowing you to direct your full attention to the task at hand. You will find that you can dive into deep work more quickly, maintain your concentration for longer periods, and experience fewer distractions that derail your train of thought. Ultimately, investing a few minutes each day into keeping your space tidy is not about achieving perfection, but about creating an environment that supports your well-being, saves your energy, and empowers you to navigate daily life with ease and efficiency.

--- RESPONSE E ---
When you maintain a tidy living space, everyday routines flow more smoothly because you spend far less time searching for misplaced items such as keys, documents, or clothing, which eliminates the small but cumulative frustrations that can derail the start of your day and leave more room for actual progress on what matters. A clean and organized environment also lowers the subtle background stress that clutter tends to create, allowing your mind to settle into a calmer state without the constant visual reminders of unfinished tasks or disorder pulling at your attention. 

This same orderliness further supports deeper concentration when you sit down to work or study, since there are fewer distractions competing for your focus and your thoughts can remain directed toward the task at hand rather than wandering to the surrounding mess, ultimately making those sessions more productive and less mentally draining. Over time, these benefits compound, turning a simple habit of tidiness into a reliable foundation for smoother, less taxing daily life.

--- END OF RESPONSES ---
Now output the JSON object described above, and nothing else.
